# API: Store

Browse and search the Store, read a listing, install and uninstall Digital Humans and skills, install from a local `.dhpkg` file, and manage Store sources and updates. Publishing happens in the Halo app; see [Publish to the Store](/en/developers/store-publishing).

Paths are relative to your Halo base URL, and every request carries the access password. Set `$HALO_URL` and `$HALO_TOKEN` as in the [quickstart](/en/developers/quickstart); base URL, authentication and error conventions are in the [HTTP API overview](/en/developers/api/).

| Operation | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |

| [Preview the slash-command name a skill title would install under](#get-api-skills-command-name) | `GET /api/skills/command-name` |

## Preview the slash-command name a skill title would install under {#get-api-skills-command-name}

`GET /api/skills/command-name` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Query: ?name=. A missing name returns an empty string, not a 400. Pure string transform — it does not check whether that name is already taken.

**Query parameters**: `name`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:string}  // e.g. "My Skill" -> "my-skill"
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/skills/command-name" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Get a listing's SKILL.md/README document {#get-api-store-app-document}

`GET /api/store/app-document` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- slug is a query param (?slug=...), not a path segment — scoped slugs like "owner/repo" contain "/". content is null when the source has no document.

**Query parameters**: `slug`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{content:string|null}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/store/app-document" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Install an app from the store by slug (REST-style path variant) {#post-api-store-apps-slug-install}

`POST /api/store/apps/:slug/install` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Always send `spaceId`. It is used exactly as sent: leave it out and the item installs for every workspace; name another workspace and it installs there. Both answer `success: true`, and the response does not say where it went.
- Send `"spaceId": null` only for a deliberate global install of a skill or MCP app. Optional field: `userConfig` (object).
- Same as [`POST /api/store/install`](#post-api-store-install) with the slug in the path, including the 403 `MCP_COMMAND_BLOCKED` case.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `slug` | Store listing slug, from [`GET /api/store/apps`](#get-api-store-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "spaceId": "<spaceId>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId}} or {success:false,error,code?}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/apps/<slug>/install" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spaceId":"<spaceId>"}'
```

## Install a digital human from a local .dhpkg file {#post-api-store-import-dhpkg}

`POST /api/store/import-dhpkg` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Installs and activates the package's Digital Human; it then runs on its own schedule. Undo with [`DELETE /api/apps/:appId`](/en/developers/api/digital-human#delete-api-apps-appid).
- Unlike installing in the Halo app or through its assistant, this does not fetch the package's required skills or undo a half-finished install. Check [`GET /api/apps/:appId`](/en/developers/api/digital-human#get-api-apps-appid) afterwards; an activation that fails after the install still answers `success: true`.
- `filePath` is a path on the computer running Halo. `spaceId` is used exactly as sent: left out means an install for every workspace, another workspace installs there, and neither is reported back.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "filePath": "/absolute/path/to/app.dhpkg",
  "spaceId": "<spaceId>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId}}
```

**Errors**

- 400 when `filePath` is missing.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/import-dhpkg" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filePath":"/absolute/path/to/app.dhpkg","spaceId":"<spaceId>"}'
```

## Install an app from the store by slug {#post-api-store-install}

`POST /api/store/install` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Always send `spaceId`. It is used exactly as sent: leave it out and the item installs for every workspace; name another workspace and it installs there. Both answer `success: true`, and the response does not say where it went.
- Send `"spaceId": null` only for a deliberate global install of a skill or MCP app. Optional field: `userConfig` (object).
- Same operation as [`POST /api/store/apps/:slug/install`](#post-api-store-apps-slug-install), with the slug in the body.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "slug": "author/app-id",
  "spaceId": "<spaceId>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId}} or {success:false,error,code?}
```

**Errors**

- 400 = missing slug.
- 403 with `code: "MCP_COMMAND_BLOCKED"` when the item is an MCP server this build's policy blocks.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/install" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug":"author/app-id","spaceId":"<spaceId>"}'
```

## Add a new registry source {#post-api-store-registries}

`POST /api/store/registries` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Optional fields: `sourceType` (string) and `adapterConfig` (object, adapter-specific, for example an API key). The response returns `adapterConfig` as stored.
- `url` must be http(s) and must not point to a loopback, private or link-local host. Fails if a source with the same URL already exists.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "name": "My Registry",
  "url": "https://example.com/registry"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{id,name,url,enabled,isDefault:false,sourceType?,adapterConfig?}} | {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/registries" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"My Registry","url":"https://example.com/registry"}'
```

## Apply an available update to an installed app {#post-api-store-updates-appid-apply}

`POST /api/store/updates/:appId/apply` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- mode is optional: "patch_minor"|"major"|"force", defaults to "force". No built-in downgrade path — reinstalling the old version is the way back.
- A digital human keeps the user's version of every field that differs from the author's new version (prompt, run schedule, name, ...); kept lists those fields, empty when the update applied in full. editsKnown false means there was no earlier author version to compare with, so every difference was kept. The user can switch kept fields to the author's version in the app.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](/en/developers/api/digital-human#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "mode": "force"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId,from,to,severity,kept,editsKnown}} or {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/updates/<appId>/apply" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"force"}'
```

## Re-check all installed apps for available updates right now {#post-api-store-updates-check-now}

`POST /api/store/updates/check-now` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Apps set to auto-update silently apply any patch/minor update found — this is not just a read.

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{appId,currentVersion,latestVersion,entry,strategy,severity}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/store/updates/check-now" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```
